cefrAlignment: B2-appropriate: writing a clear email that conveys information, makes requests and proposes solutions in a register suited to the reader matches the CEFR B2 correspondence descriptors.
examFidelity: Consistent with exams.ts: one Write an Email task, 7 minutes, academic or social situation, with a prompt listing what the email must do; the 80–100 word target matches the exams.ts strategy line and the content guide.
fixes: Model email: 'two extra days' did not match a Thursday-to-Monday delay; changed to 'a little more time'
ex4 Q2: removed the option 'Saying when the exam is', which was not a task point but was also not covered, so a learner could defend it; the question now offers only the three task points

ex3 gaps: added grammatical alternatives (possible: OK/okay/convenient; option: possibility/alternative/idea/solution/suggestion; inconvenience: trouble/difficulty/disruption/delay/problems; information: help/assistance)
openConcerns: ETS does not publish a minimum word count for Write an Email; the 80–100 word target comes from exams.ts strategy guidance, and third-party guides vary (about 80–150 words)
learnerOutcome: A learner can plan and write a complete, well-pitched email in 7 minutes that covers every required point with specific detail and a polite proposal.
